basis: Craniosynostosis, alopecia and brain defects define the syndrome; skeletal, cutaneous and neurologic axes apply.
Glycosylation disorder; developmental delay 7/7, hepatic abnormalities 9/9 with cholestasis 5/9, thrombocytopenia 5/5. Sweat/skin and cardiac defects omitted by cap.
Inflammation of the orbital periosteum affects the eye adnexa and bone covering; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent skeletal deformities and muscle atrophy occur in 80-99%, sensorineural hearing loss in 3/7. Transaminases alone do not establish liver injury.
Invasive glandular epithelial malignancy originating in the colon.
Acute ischemic necrosis of the inferoposterior myocardium.
Inherited epidermal barrier and keratinization disorder. Associated asthma is a separate disease, not direct pulmonary damage from ichthyosis.
Congenital renal agenesis, hypoplasia or dysplasia; uterine abnormalities have no applicable axis.
Carcinoma originating in bronchial epithelial and myoepithelial structures.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood characterized by monosomy 5.
HPV-associated giant condylomatous/verrucous tumour of anogenital skin or mucosa. Anal mucosal origin applies to a site-specific subset.
Exostoses and skull ossification defects define the syndrome; developmental delay 80-99% and intellectual disability 7/10. Persistent strabismus/nystagmus occur in 30-79%.
Photosensitive dermatosis and immunodeficiency define the syndrome. Malignancies, diabetes, reflux and otitis are separately diagnosed conditions, not additional organ labels.
Localized dermal atrophy with depressed hyperpigmented plaques. Proposed links to morphea or Borrelia do not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Acute bacterial infection of the endometrium; the uterine site has no organ axis, but the infection mechanism applies.
Renal tubular aldosterone resistance defines an electrolyte and acid-base disorder with salt wasting and hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis.
Chronic calcifying injury of the exocrine pancreas. Associated pancreatogenic diabetes and pancreatic cancer are separately diagnosed diseases.
Hydrocephalus and skeletal malformations define HYLS1 disease; microphthalmia 49/56, tracheal stenosis 29/38 and laryngeal hypoplasia 32/56 support eye and airway involvement.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder causing paroxysmal ventricular fibrillation.
Disease of the pulmonary arteries belongs to the vascular axis; airway or lung parenchymal injury is not established by this umbrella concept.
Brain malformations and vision-impairing ocular coloboma define the syndrome. Central breathing abnormalities do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Caustic oral/GI injury and destructive pulmonary toxicity are characteristic; direct tubular renal injury occurs in roughly half. Hepatic injury varies with dose; ≥30% is uncertain.
Ischemic necrosis directly damages liver parenchyma; a separate vessel lesion is not specified.
Ectodermal dysplasia with blindness defines cutaneous appendage and ocular involvement; additional organ defects are not documented.
Umbrella disorder of cutaneous sebaceous glands; ocular or infectious subtypes do not characterize the group as a whole.
